records.source: אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙ לִֽידִידִ֔י שִׁירַ֥ת דּוֹדִ֖י לְכַרְמ֑וֹ כֶּ֛רֶם הָיָ֥ה לִֽידִידִ֖י בְּקֶ֥רֶן בֶּן־שָֽׁמֶן׃
records.gloss: Let me sing please for my beloved a song of my beloved for his vineyard. A vineyard belonged to my beloved on a horn, a son of oil.
pieces: Let me sing a song for my dear friend, my friend's song about his vineyard: \q My friend owned a vineyard on a hilltop rich in soil.

L.1: Let me sing, please, for my beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard. \q A vineyard belonged to my beloved on a horn, a son of oil.

R.1: I will sing a song for my dear friend, a song about his vineyard. \q My friend had a vineyard on a hill with rich soil.

decisions.choice: my beloved: the singer's dear friend, who will turn out to be the LORD
decisions.reason: Two related words are used, both meaning one who is loved, a dear friend; the second is used in the Song of Songs for the bride's beloved. The prophet sings like a friend of the bridegroom about his friend's vineyard. Only verse 7 reveals that the friend is the LORD of hosts and the vineyard is his people.

decisions.choice: a song of my beloved: a love song, or a song about my friend
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean a song about the beloved or a love song. In the Song of Songs a vineyard is a picture of the beloved woman (Song 1:6; 8:12), so hearers would first expect a love song.

decisions.choice: on a horn, a son of oil: on a fertile hilltop
decisions.reason: A "horn" is a hill or spur that juts out; "son of oil" means rich, fat ground. The vineyard had the best site possible.

decisions.choice: my dear friend
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "my dear friend" so the song does not sound like a sweetheart's song; Literal keeps "my beloved". The friend is a figure in a song, so the pronouns for him are not capitalized, even though verse 7 shows him to be the LORD.

records.heading: A song about my friend's vineyard

records.source: וַֽיְעַזְּקֵ֣הוּ וַֽיְסַקְּלֵ֗הוּ וַיִּטָּעֵ֨הוּ֙ שֹׂרֵ֔ק וַיִּ֤בֶן מִגְדָּל֙ בְּתוֹכ֔וֹ וְגַם־יֶ֖קֶב חָצֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ וַיְקַ֛ו לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עֲנָבִ֖ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בְּאֻשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And he dug it and he cleared it of stones and he planted it [with] choice vine, and he built a tower in its midst, and also a wine vat he hewed in it; and he waited [for it] to make grapes, and it made stinking [grapes].
pieces: He broke up its soil, removed the stones, and set out vines of the finest kind. \q He built a tower in the middle of it and also hewed out a wine vat there. \q He waited for it to bear grapes, but what it bore was stinking fruit.

L.2: And he dug it and cleared it of stones and planted it [with] choice vines, \q and he built a tower in its midst, and also a wine vat he hewed out in it; \q and he waited [for it] to produce grapes, and it produced stinking [ones].

R.2: He dug up the ground and took out the stones. He planted the very best vines. \q He built a watchtower in the middle of the vineyard. He also cut a pit in the rock to press the grapes. \q He waited for good grapes to grow. But only bad, sour grapes grew there.

decisions.choice: dug, cleared, tower, wine vat: everything a careful owner could do
decisions.reason: Hillside ground had to be broken up and cleared of stones before planting. A stone tower let a watchman guard the ripening grapes, and a vat cut into the rock was where the grapes were trodden. The owner did not build a mere hut (1:8) but a tower, and expected a harvest.

decisions.choice: choice vines: vines of the best kind
decisions.reason: The word names a fine, perhaps red, variety of grapevine (Jeremiah 2:21, where God says he planted Israel as a choice vine).

decisions.choice: stinking grapes: grapes that are rotten or worthless
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning "to stink". It is often rendered "wild grapes", but it more likely means grapes that went bad, sour and worthless.

decisions.choice: watchtower ... a pit in the rock to press the grapes
decisions.reason: Readable says what the tower and the wine vat were for.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֛ה יוֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֑ה שִׁפְטוּ־נָ֕א בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין כַּרְמִֽי׃
records.gloss: And now, inhabitant of Jerusalem and man of Judah, judge please between me and between my vineyard.
pieces: Now then, people of Jerusalem and {{gender:people|men}} of Judah, \q be the judges between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard.

L.3: And now, inhabitant of Jerusalem and man of Judah, \q judge, please, between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard.

R.3: Now, you who live in Jerusalem and Judah, \q you decide who is right, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard.

decisions.choice: me ... my vineyard: the owner himself now speaks
decisions.reason: The singer stops and the owner of the vineyard speaks in his own voice. Verse 6 will show that the speaker is God, since only God commands the clouds.

decisions.choice: judge between me and my vineyard: a court case
decisions.reason: The hearers are asked to judge the case, as Nathan led David to judge himself (2 Samuel 12:1-7). By agreeing that the vineyard deserves its fate, they will pass judgment on themselves (verse 7).

decisions.choice: people of Jerusalem / you who live in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "Inhabitant" and "man" are singulars meaning everyone who lives there, so Balanced and Readable use plurals.

records.source: מַה־לַּעֲשׂ֥וֹת עוֹד֙ לְכַרְמִ֔י וְלֹ֥א עָשִׂ֖יתִי בּ֑וֹ מַדּ֧וּעַ קִוֵּ֛יתִי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עֲנָבִ֖ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בְּאֻשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: What [was there] to do more for my vineyard and not I have done in it? Why, I waited [for it] to make grapes, and it made stinking [grapes]?
pieces: What else could I have done for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard that I left undone? \q I waited for it to bear grapes; why did it bear stinking ones?

L.4: What more [was there] to do for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard that I have not done in it? \q Why, [when] I waited [for it] to produce grapes, did it produce stinking [ones]?

R.4: Is there anything else I could have done for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard? I have done everything! \q I waited for good grapes. So why did it grow only bad grapes?

decisions.choice: what more ... why: questions that expect no answer
decisions.reason: The first question means that nothing more could have been done. The second asks the hearers to find any fault in the owner; there is none (Jeremiah 2:5; Micah 6:3).

decisions.choice: I have done everything!
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the first question expects.

records.source: וְעַתָּה֙ אוֹדִֽיעָה־נָּ֣א אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֖ה לְכַרְמִ֑י הָסֵ֤ר מְשׂוּכָּתוֹ֙ וְהָיָ֣ה לְבָעֵ֔ר פָּרֹ֥ץ גְּדֵר֖וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְמִרְמָֽס׃
records.gloss: And now let me make know please you what I [am] doing to my vineyard: removing its hedge, and it will be for grazing; breaking down its wall, and it will be for trampling.
pieces: So now I will let you know what I mean to do to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard: \q I will pull up its hedge so that it is grazed bare; \q I will knock down its wall so that it is trampled.

L.5: And now let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} make known, please, to you what I am doing to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard: \q removing its hedge, and it will be for grazing; \q breaking down its wall, and it will be for trampling.

R.5: Now I will tell you what I am going to do to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard. \q I will tear out the hedge around it, and animals will eat it up. \q I will break down its wall, and it will be stamped flat.

decisions.choice: for grazing: eaten down by animals
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to burn or to graze. Next to "trampling" it most likely means that animals will graze the vineyard bare (3:14 uses it of the leaders who "devoured" the vineyard).

decisions.choice: hedge ... wall: the vineyard's protection
decisions.reason: A thorn hedge and a stone wall kept animals and thieves out (Psalm 80:13-14). Without them the vineyard is open to anyone.

decisions.choice: animals will eat it up
decisions.reason: Readable names the animals that graze.

records.source: וַאֲשִׁיתֵ֣הוּ בָתָ֗ה לֹ֤א יִזָּמֵר֙ וְלֹ֣א יֵעָדֵ֔ר וְעָלָ֥ה שָׁמִ֖יר וָשָׁ֑יִת וְעַ֤ל הֶעָבִים֙ אֲצַוֶּ֔ה מֵהַמְטִ֥יר עָלָ֖יו מָטָֽר׃
records.gloss: And I will make it a waste; not it will be pruned and not it will be hoed, and will come up thorn and brier; and on the clouds I will command from raining on it rain.
pieces: I will lay it waste. No one will prune it or hoe around its vines; \q thorns and briers will spring up. \q I will even forbid the clouds to drop rain on it.

L.6: And I will make it a waste; it will not be pruned and it will not be hoed, \q and thorn and brier will come up; \q and I will command the clouds from raining rain on it.

R.6: I will let it be ruined. No one will cut back its branches or dig the soil. \q Weeds and thorns will grow there. \q I will even order the clouds not to rain on it.

decisions.choice: I will command the clouds: the owner is God
decisions.reason: No farmer can stop the rain. With these words the song shows who the owner is before verse 7 says it (1 Kings 17:1; Amos 4:7).

decisions.choice: thorn and brier: land gone wild
decisions.reason: This pair of words is used only by Isaiah (7:23-25; 9:17; 10:17; 27:4) for farmland left to ruin.

decisions.choice: No one will prune it or hoe around its vines
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the two passives into one clause with "no one"; Literal keeps "it will not be pruned and it will not be hoed".

records.source: כִּ֣י כֶ֜רֶם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה נְטַ֖ע שַׁעֲשׁוּעָ֑יו וַיְקַ֤ו לְמִשְׁפָּט֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשְׂפָּ֔ח לִצְדָקָ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה צְעָקָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: For [the] vineyard of Yahweh of hosts [is the] house of Israel, and [the] man of Judah [the] planting of his delight; and he waited for justice, and look, bloodshed; for righteousness, and look, an outcry.
pieces: The vineyard of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is the house of Israel, \q and the people of Judah are the planting that delighted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q He waited for justice, but what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found was bloodshed; \q for righteousness, but what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard was a cry of the wronged.

L.7: For the vineyard of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] the house of Israel, \q and the man of Judah [is] the planting of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} delight; \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} waited for justice, and look, bloodshed; \q for righteousness, and look, an outcry.

R.7: Here is what the song means. Israel is the vineyard of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. The people of Judah are the garden {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved. \q He waited for justice, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw people being killed. \q He waited for righteousness, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard people crying for help.

decisions.choice: the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel: the song explained
decisions.reason: The hearers who agreed to judge the vineyard (verse 3) now learn that they are the vineyard. Israel is pictured as God's vine or vineyard elsewhere too (Psalm 80:9-17; Jeremiah 2:21; 12:10; Isaiah 27:2-6), and Jesus takes up this song in Mark 12:1-12.

decisions.choice: justice / bloodshed, righteousness / outcry: a play on words
decisions.reason: The verse ends with two plays on sound. The word for "bloodshed" sounds almost the same as "justice", and the word for "outcry" differs from "righteousness" by one letter. God looked for one thing and found what sounds like it but is its opposite. The "outcry" is the cry of people who are wronged, the cry that reaches God (Genesis 18:20-21; Exodus 3:7, 9).

decisions.choice: he waited ... and look: the same verb as in verses 2 and 4
decisions.reason: "He waited" repeats the verb used of the owner waiting for grapes. "Look" marks what he found instead, with a note of shock.

decisions.choice: what he found / he saw ... what he heard / he heard
decisions.reason: "Look" introduces each surprise; Balanced and Readable say "found" or "saw" for the bloodshed and "heard" for the outcry, since a cry is heard. The sound play cannot be kept without changing the sense, so the footnote explains it.

decisions.choice: Here is what the song means
decisions.reason: The opening "for" introduces the explanation of the song; Readable says so.

records.source: ה֗וֹי מַגִּיעֵ֥י בַ֨יִת֙ בְּבַ֔יִת שָׂדֶ֥ה בְשָׂדֶ֖ה יַקְרִ֑יבוּ עַ֚ד אֶ֣פֶס מָק֔וֹם וְהֽוּשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם לְבַדְּכֶ֖ם בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Woe [those who] make touch house with house, field with field they bring near, until there is not room, and you are made to dwell, you alone, in [the] midst of the land.
pieces: Woe to those who buy up house after house and attach field after field, \q until no room is left and you are settled all alone in the heart of the land.

L.8: Woe, [those who] join house to house, field to field they bring near, \q until there is no room, and you are made to dwell alone in the midst of the land!

R.8: How terrible it will be for you who keep buying houses and fields! \q You buy until there is no land left for anyone else. Then you live all alone in the land.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of mourning, announcing judgment
decisions.reason: The word is the cry made over the dead (1 Kings 13:30; Jeremiah 22:18). Six times in this chapter (verses 8, 11, 18, 20, 21, 22) the prophet raises it over the living, as if they were already dead.

decisions.choice: joining house to house and field to field: the rich take over the land
decisions.reason: Each family's land was its share in God's land and was not to be sold for good (Leviticus 25:23; Numbers 36:7). The rich bought up or seized the land of the poor (Micah 2:2; 1 Kings 21).

decisions.choice: you are made to dwell alone: the speaker turns to address them
decisions.reason: The verse begins by speaking about "those who" and ends by speaking to "you". Such shifts are common in the woe sayings.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for
decisions.reason: Readable says "How terrible it will be for" for "woe", a cry of mourning that announces coming disaster (see the note at verse 8).

records.heading: Woe after woe

records.source: בְּאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם־לֹ֞א בָּתִּ֤ים רַבִּים֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה יִֽהְי֔וּ גְּדֹלִ֥ים וְטוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃
records.gloss: In my ears Yahweh of hosts: if not houses many to a desolation will become, great and good [ones], without inhabitant.
pieces: In my hearing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sworn: \q Many houses will surely be left in ruins, large, fine houses standing empty, with no one to live in them.

L.9: In my ears [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q surely many houses will become a desolation, great and fine [ones] without inhabitant.

R.9: I heard {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies make this promise: \q Many houses will be ruined. Big, beautiful houses will stand empty.

decisions.choice: in my ears the LORD of hosts: the prophet heard God speak
decisions.reason: The verb is left out: the LORD spoke, or swore, in the prophet's hearing (22:14). The verse is short and blunt.

decisions.choice: if not: surely, a form of oath
decisions.reason: "If not" begins an oath, with a curse left unspoken: "may it be so with me if this does not happen". It means "surely".

decisions.choice: houses without inhabitant: the punishment fits the sin
decisions.reason: Those who bought up houses (verse 8) will see them stand empty (6:11; Deuteronomy 28:30; Amos 5:11).

decisions.choice: has sworn / make this promise
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb the Hebrew leaves out; the oath form in the verse shows it is a sworn word.

records.source: כִּ֗י עֲשֶׂ֨רֶת֙ צִמְדֵּי־כֶ֔רֶם יַעֲשׂ֖וּ בַּ֣ת אֶחָ֑ת וְזֶ֥רַע חֹ֖מֶר יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֵיפָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: For ten yokes of vineyard will make a bath one, and seed of a homer will make an ephah.
pieces: Ten {{units:acres|yokes}} of vineyard will yield only {{units:about 6 gallons|one bath}} of wine, \q and {{units:about 6 bushels|a homer}} of seed will produce only {{units:about half a bushel|an ephah}} of grain.

L.10: For ten yokes of vineyard will produce one bath, \q and a homer of seed will produce an ephah.

R.10: Ten {{units:acres|yokes}} of grapevines will make only {{units:about 6 gallons|one bath}} of wine. \q {{units:About 6 bushels|A homer}} of seed will grow only {{units:about half a bushel|an ephah}} of grain.

decisions.choice: yoke, bath, homer, ephah: measures of land and harvest
decisions.reason: A "yoke" is the land a pair of oxen can plow in a day, roughly an acre. A bath is a liquid measure of about 6 gallons, a homer a dry measure of about 6 bushels, and an ephah a tenth of a homer (Ezekiel 45:11). So the harvest will be a tenth of the seed sown, and a large vineyard will give almost no wine.

decisions.choice: acres, gallons, bushels
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give rough modern measures, with the Hebrew measures as the setting. Literal keeps the Hebrew measures.

decisions.choice: only ... of wine ... of grain
decisions.reason: The point is how little the land yields, so Balanced and Readable add "only" and name what is measured.

records.source: ה֛וֹי מַשְׁכִּימֵ֥י בַבֹּ֖קֶר שֵׁכָ֣ר יִרְדֹּ֑פוּ מְאַחֲרֵ֣י בַנֶּ֔שֶׁף יַ֖יִן יַדְלִיקֵֽם׃
records.gloss: Woe [those who] rise early in the morning, strong drink they pursue, [those who] stay late in the twilight, wine inflames them.
pieces: Woe to those who get up at dawn to chase after beer, \q who linger late into the evening until wine sets them on fire.

L.11: Woe, [those who] rise early in the morning [that] they may pursue strong drink, \q [who] stay late into the evening [while] wine inflames them!

R.11: How terrible it will be for people who get up early to drink beer! \q They stay up late at night until the wine makes them wild.

decisions.choice: strong drink: beer or other fermented drink
decisions.reason: The word means an intoxicating drink other than wine, most often beer made from grain. It is regularly paired with wine (verse 22; 28:7).

decisions.choice: from early morning until late evening: drinking all day
decisions.reason: Drinking in the morning was a sign of a life given over to pleasure (Ecclesiastes 10:16). The word for evening means the dusk or twilight, when the day cools.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for
decisions.reason: Readable says "How terrible it will be for" for "woe", a cry of mourning that announces coming disaster (see the note at verse 8).

records.source: וְהָיָ֨ה כִנּ֜וֹר וָנֶ֗בֶל תֹּ֧ף וְחָלִ֛יל וָיַ֖יִן מִשְׁתֵּיהֶ֑ם וְאֵ֨ת פֹּ֤עַל יְהוָה֙ לֹ֣א יַבִּ֔יטוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדָ֖יו לֹ֥א רָאֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And are harp and lyre, tambourine and flute and wine their feasts; and the deed of Yahweh not they regard, and the work of his hands not they see.
pieces: Lyre and harp, tambourine and flute, and wine fill their banquets, \q but they pay no attention to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is doing \q and do not notice the work of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands.

L.12: And harp and lyre, tambourine and flute and wine are their feasts; \q but the deed of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they do not regard, \q and the work of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands they do not see.

R.12: At their parties they have music and wine. \q But they do not pay attention to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is doing. \q They do not see the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is working out.

decisions.choice: the deed of the LORD, the work of his hands: what God is doing in their history
decisions.reason: Not creation here but God's acts in the events of the time, including the judgment he is bringing (10:12; 28:21). Those who feast give it no thought (Amos 6:4-6).

decisions.choice: harp, lyre, tambourine, flute: the music of a banquet
decisions.reason: Stringed instruments, a hand drum and a pipe. The same instruments belong to worship elsewhere (1 Samuel 10:5); here they serve only pleasure.

decisions.choice: the things he is working out
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "the work of his hands" means here.

records.source: לָכֵ֛ן גָּלָ֥ה עַמִּ֖י מִבְּלִי־דָ֑עַת וּכְבוֹדוֹ֙ מְתֵ֣י רָעָ֔ב וַהֲמוֹנ֖וֹ צִחֵ֥ה צָמָֽא׃
records.gloss: Therefore has gone into exile my people from not knowledge, and its honored [ones are] men of hunger, and its multitude parched [with] thirst.
pieces: That is why {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will be carried off into exile, because they do not know. \q Their leading men will starve, \q and the common crowd will faint from thirst.

L.13: Therefore {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have gone into exile for lack of knowledge, \q and its honored [ones are] men of hunger, \q and its crowd [is] parched with thirst.

R.13: So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will be taken away as prisoners to another land, because they do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q Their important leaders will go hungry. \q All the other people will be very thirsty.

decisions.choice: has gone into exile: a future event spoken of as already done
alternatives: my people have gone into exile
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act, but the exile is still to come. Prophets often speak of what God has decided as if it had already happened. It may also refer to the northern tribes already taken by Assyria (2 Kings 15:29).

decisions.choice: for lack of knowledge: because they do not know God
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "unawares" or "because they have no knowledge". The second fits verse 12: they do not see what the LORD is doing (1:3; Hosea 4:6).

decisions.choice: my people: God speaking
decisions.reason: God speaks of "my people" as in 1:3 and 3:12, though the prophet could also be the speaker.

decisions.choice: taken away as prisoners to another land ... do not know me
decisions.reason: Readable explains exile and says whom they fail to know, as the note says.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן הִרְחִ֤יבָה שְּׁאוֹל֙ נַפְשָׁ֔הּ וּפָעֲרָ֥ה פִ֖יהָ לִבְלִי־חֹ֑ק וְיָרַ֨ד הֲדָרָ֧הּ וַהֲמוֹנָ֛הּ וּשְׁאוֹנָ֖הּ וְעָלֵ֥ז בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore has enlarged Sheol its throat and has opened its mouth without limit, and will go down her splendor and her multitude and her uproar and [one] exulting in her.
pieces: So Sheol has stretched its throat wide and opened its jaws beyond measure, \q and down into it go the city's nobles and its crowds, its noisy throng and all who revel in it.

L.14: Therefore Sheol has enlarged its throat and opened its mouth beyond limit, \q and down go her splendor and her crowd and her uproar and [whoever] exults in her.

R.14: So the grave is like a hungry animal. It has opened its mouth as wide as it can. \q Jerusalem's leaders will go down into it with all the crowds, all their noise and all their partying.

decisions.choice: Sheol ... its throat: the world of the dead as a greedy mouth
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of the dead. The word for "throat" also means appetite. Death is pictured as never full (Proverbs 27:20; 30:15-16; Habakkuk 2:5).

decisions.choice: her splendor ... in her: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The pronouns are feminine and refer to the city, Jerusalem, whose nobles and crowds were named in verse 13.

decisions.choice: splendor ... uproar: the nobility and the noisy revelry
decisions.reason: "Splendor" may mean the city's honored men; "uproar" is the noise of crowds and feasting (22:2). All of it goes down to the dead.

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Readable says "the grave" for Sheol, the world of the dead.

decisions.choice: the city's nobles / Jerusalem's leaders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the city and say what "her splendor" refers to; Readable compares Sheol's open mouth to a hungry animal.

records.source: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ח אָדָ֖ם וַיִּשְׁפַּל־אִ֑ישׁ וְעֵינֵ֥י גְבֹהִ֖ים תִּשְׁפַּֽלְנָה׃
records.gloss: And is bowed down humankind and is brought low man, and [the] eyes of [the] proud will be brought low.
pieces: So humankind is bowed down, each person is made low, \q and proud eyes are cast down.

L.15: And humankind is bowed down, and man is brought low, \q and the eyes of the proud will be brought low.

R.15: People will be humbled. Everyone will be brought low. \q Proud people will look down in shame.

decisions.choice: humankind is bowed down: the refrain of chapter 2
decisions.reason: The same words close the sayings of 2:9, 2:11 and 2:17. The day of the LORD brings down all human pride.

decisions.choice: each person / everyone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word "man" here means every person, as in 2:9.

records.source: וַיִּגְבַּ֛היְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וְהָאֵל֙ הַקָּד֔וֹשׁ נִקְדָּ֖שׁ בִּצְדָקָֽה׃
records.gloss: And is exalted Yahweh of hosts in justice, and the God the holy shows himself holy in righteousness.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies stands high in justice, \q and the holy God shows that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is holy by acting in righteousness.

L.16: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts is exalted in justice, \q and the holy God shows {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} holy in righteousness.

R.16: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will be honored when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judges fairly. \q The holy God will show that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is holy by doing what is right.

decisions.choice: exalted ... shows himself holy: God is shown to be who he is
decisions.reason: As people are brought low (verse 15), the LORD alone is lifted up (2:11, 17). When God judges justly, he shows his holiness for all to see (Ezekiel 28:22; 38:23).

decisions.choice: justice, righteousness: the qualities God looked for in verse 7
decisions.reason: The same pair as in verse 7. God found no justice or righteousness in his people, so he shows his own by judging them.

decisions.choice: by doing what is right
decisions.reason: Readable says what acting in righteousness means; Literal and Balanced keep "righteousness".

records.source: וְרָע֥וּ כְבָשִׂ֖ים כְּדָבְרָ֑ם וְחָרְב֥וֹת מֵחִ֖ים גָּרִ֥ים יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: And will graze lambs as [in] their pasture, and [the] ruins of fat ones sojourners will eat.
pieces: Lambs will graze there as in their own pasture, \q and strangers will feed among the ruins of the rich.

L.17: And lambs will graze as [in] their pasture, \q and the ruins of the fat ones sojourners will eat.

R.17: Lambs will eat grass there as if it were their own field. \q Strangers will eat in the ruins where rich people once lived.

decisions.choice: the ruins of the fat ones: the wrecked estates of the rich
decisions.reason: "Fat ones" is used of fattened animals and, as a picture, of the rich and well fed (Psalm 22:30; Ezekiel 34:16). Where the great houses stood, animals will graze.

decisions.choice: sojourners: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means people who live as foreigners in a land. The Septuagint reads the line differently, with lambs as the ones who eat the abandoned places, which fits the first half of the verse.

records.source: ה֛וֹי מֹשְׁכֵ֥י הֶֽעָוֺ֖ן בְּחַבְלֵ֣י הַשָּׁ֑וְא וְכַעֲב֥וֹת הָעֲגָלָ֖ה חַטָּאָֽה׃
records.gloss: Woe [those who] drag the iniquity with cords of emptiness, and like [the] rope of the cart, sin,
pieces: Woe to those who tow their guilt behind them with ropes of falsehood \q and haul their sin along as though hitched to a cart.

L.18: Woe, [those who] drag iniquity with cords of falsehood, \q and like the ropes of a cart, sin,

R.18: How terrible it will be for people who pull their sin along behind them! \q They are tied to it by lies, like an animal tied to a cart.

decisions.choice: dragging sin with ropes: bound to their sin and pulling it along
decisions.reason: The picture may be of people harnessed to their sin like animals to a cart, or of people working hard to bring their sin, and its punishment, ever closer. The word for "iniquity" can also mean the punishment it brings.

decisions.choice: emptiness: falsehood, worthlessness
decisions.reason: The word means what is empty, false or worthless (1:13; Exodus 20:7).

decisions.choice: like an animal tied to a cart
decisions.reason: Readable names the animal that pulls a cart, to make the picture clear.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for
decisions.reason: Readable says "How terrible it will be for" for "woe", a cry of mourning that announces coming disaster (see the note at verse 8).

records.source: הָאֹמְרִ֗ים יְמַהֵ֧ר׀יָחִ֛ישָׁה מַעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ לְמַ֣עַן נִרְאֶ֑ה וְתִקְרַ֣ב וְתָב֗וֹאָה עֲצַ֛ת קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְנֵדָֽעָה׃ס
records.gloss: who say, let it hurry, let it make haste, his work, so that we may see; and let draw near and let come [the] plan of [the] Holy One of Israel, so that we may know.
pieces: They say, "Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be quick and hurry up with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work, so we can see it! \q May the plan of the Holy One of Israel draw near and arrive, so we can know it!"

L.19: who say, "Let it hurry, let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work make haste, so that we may see [it]; \q and let the plan of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, so that we may know [it]!"

R.19: They make fun of God and say, "Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} hurry up and do {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work. Then we will see it! \q Let the Holy One of Israel carry out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan. Then we will know about it!"

decisions.choice: his work ... the plan of the Holy One of Israel: they mock God's warnings
decisions.reason: "Work" and "plan" are what the prophet has said God will do in judgment (verse 12; 28:21-22). The scoffers dare God to act; they do not believe he will (Jeremiah 17:15; 2 Peter 3:3-4). They even use the prophet's own title for God, "the Holy One of Israel" (1:4).

decisions.choice: let it hurry: the subject is "his work"
alternatives: let him hurry, let him speed his work
decisions.reason: The two verbs may both have "his work" as subject, or the first may mean "let him hurry". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Let him be quick
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make God the subject of the hurrying, which the Hebrew allows; see the note on grammar.

decisions.choice: They make fun of God
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of speech this is.

records.source: ה֣וֹי הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לָרַ֛ע ט֖וֹב וְלַטּ֣וֹב רָ֑ע שָׂמִ֨ים חֹ֤שֶׁךְ לְאוֹר֙ וְא֣וֹר לְחֹ֔שֶׁךְ שָׂמִ֥ים מַ֛ר לְמָת֖וֹק וּמָת֥וֹק לְמָֽר׃ס
records.gloss: Woe [those who] say of evil good and of good evil, [who] put darkness for light and light for darkness, [who] put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter.
pieces: Woe to those who name evil as good and good as evil, \q who turn darkness into light and light into darkness, \q who turn bitter into sweet and sweet into bitter.

L.20: Woe, [those who] say of evil, good, and of good, evil, \q who put darkness for light and light for darkness, \q who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter!

R.20: How terrible it will be for people who say that evil things are good and good things are evil! \q They act as if dark were light and light were dark. \q They act as if bitter were sweet and sweet were bitter.

decisions.choice: calling evil good: turning God's standards upside down
decisions.reason: The three pairs say the same thing three ways: such people reverse right and wrong (Proverbs 17:15; Amos 5:7). It prepares for verse 23, where judges declare the guilty innocent.

decisions.choice: name evil as good / turn darkness into light
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "name" for "say of" and "turn into" for "put for"; Literal keeps the Hebrew wording.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for
decisions.reason: Readable says "How terrible it will be for" for "woe", a cry of mourning that announces coming disaster (see the note at verse 8).

records.source: ה֖וֹי חֲכָמִ֣ים בְּעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְנֶ֥גֶד פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם נְבֹנִֽים׃
records.gloss: Woe [those] wise in their own eyes, and before their own faces discerning.
pieces: Woe to those who are wise in their own view \q and shrewd as they see themselves.

L.21: Woe, [those] wise in their own eyes, \q and discerning before their own faces!

R.21: How terrible it will be for people who think they are wise \q and believe they are very clever!

decisions.choice: wise in their own eyes: wisdom that does not fear God
decisions.reason: Proverbs warns against being wise in one's own eyes (Proverbs 3:7; 26:12). True wisdom begins with the fear of the LORD (Proverbs 1:7; Isaiah 11:2).

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for
decisions.reason: Readable says "How terrible it will be for" for "woe", a cry of mourning that announces coming disaster (see the note at verse 8).

records.source: ה֕וֹי גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים לִשְׁתּ֣וֹת יָ֑יִן וְאַנְשֵׁי־חַ֖יִל לִמְסֹ֥ךְ שֵׁכָֽר׃
records.gloss: Woe [those] mighty at drinking wine, and men of strength at mixing strong drink,
pieces: Woe to the mighty warriors of the wine cup, \q the valiant men who excel at blending strong drink,

L.22: Woe, [those] mighty at drinking wine, \q and men of valor at mixing strong drink,

R.22: How terrible it will be for people who are proud of how much wine they can drink \q and how well they can mix strong drinks!

decisions.choice: mighty, men of valor: words for warriors, used in mockery
decisions.reason: Both terms are used of brave soldiers. These men are brave only at the table. Verses 22 and 23 may describe the same leaders: those who should defend the people spend their strength on drink.

decisions.choice: mixing: blending wine with spices
decisions.reason: Wine was mixed with spices or other drinks to make it stronger (Proverbs 9:2; 23:30; Song 8:2).

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for
decisions.reason: Readable says "How terrible it will be for" for "woe", a cry of mourning that announces coming disaster (see the note at verse 8).

records.source: מַצְדִּיקֵ֥י רָשָׁ֖ע עֵ֣קֶב שֹׁ֑חַד וְצִדְקַ֥ת צַדִּיקִ֖ים יָסִ֥ירוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃ס
records.gloss: [who] justify a wicked [one] for a bribe, and [the] righteousness of [the] righteous they take away from him.
pieces: who declare the guilty innocent in exchange for a bribe \q and rob the righteous of their righteous cause.

L.23: [who] declare the wicked righteous for a bribe, \q and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him.

R.23: They take bribes and say that guilty people are innocent. \q They take away the rights of people who have done nothing wrong.

decisions.choice: declaring the wicked righteous for a bribe: corrupt judges
decisions.reason: "Justify" is a court word: to declare someone in the right. Taking bribes to do so was forbidden in the law (Exodus 23:7-8; Deuteronomy 16:19; Isaiah 1:23).

decisions.choice: the righteousness of the righteous: their right standing in court
decisions.reason: Here "righteousness" is the innocent person's just claim, his right to be declared in the right.

decisions.choice: the guilty innocent / rights
decisions.reason: In a court case "wicked" and "righteous" mean guilty and innocent; Balanced and Readable use the court words. Readable says "rights" for "righteousness" as explained in the note.

records.source: לָכֵן֩ כֶּאֱכֹ֨ל קַ֜שׁ לְשׁ֣וֹן אֵ֗שׁ וַחֲשַׁ֤שׁ לֶֽהָבָה֙ יִרְפֶּ֔ה שָׁרְשָׁם֙ כַּמָּ֣ק יִֽהְיֶ֔ה וּפִרְחָ֖ם כָּאָבָ֣ק יַעֲלֶ֑ה כִּ֣י מָאֲס֗וּ אֵ֚ת תּוֹרַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְאֵ֛ת אִמְרַ֥ת קְדֽוֹשׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִאֵֽצוּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore, as consumes stubble a tongue of fire, and dry grass in the flame sinks down, their root like rot will be, and their blossom like dust will go up; for they have rejected the instruction of Yahweh of hosts, and the word of the Holy One of Israel they have spurned.
pieces: So, just as flames devour stubble and dry grass collapses into the fire, \q their root will turn to rot and their blossom will rise like dust, \q because they have thrown away the instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies \q and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

L.24: Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes stubble, and dry grass sinks down in the flame, \q their root will be like rot, and their blossom will go up like dust; \q for they have rejected the instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q and the word of the Holy One of Israel they have spurned.

R.24: So they will be destroyed like straw and dry grass in a fire. \q They will be like a plant whose roots rot and whose flowers blow away like dust. \q This will happen because they refused the teaching of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q They looked down on the word of the Holy One of Israel.

decisions.choice: root and blossom: the whole plant, the whole people
decisions.reason: Root and blossom together mean all of it, from bottom to top (Amos 2:9; Malachi 3:19). The picture returns to the vineyard of verses 1-7: the plant God tended is ruined.

decisions.choice: instruction: God's teaching, the law
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or direction. Here, paired with "the word", it is what God taught his people, both in the law and through the prophets (1:10; 2:3).

decisions.choice: they will be destroyed ... They will be like a plant
decisions.reason: Readable states who is destroyed and makes the comparison with a plant explicit.

records.heading: Anger that has not turned back

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֡ן חָרָה֩ אַף־יְהוָ֨ה בְּעַמּ֜וֹ וַיֵּ֣ט יָד֧וֹ עָלָ֣יו וַיַּכֵּ֗הוּ וַֽיִּרְגְּזוּ֙ הֶֽהָרִ֔ים וַתְּהִ֧י נִבְלָתָ֛ם כַּסּוּחָ֖ה בְּקֶ֣רֶב חוּצ֑וֹת בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore has burned [the] anger of Yahweh against his people, and he has stretched out his hand against it and has struck it, and have quaked the mountains, and was their corpse like refuse in [the] middle of [the] streets. For all this not has turned back his anger, and still his hand [is] stretched out.
pieces: That is why the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blazes against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. He has raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand against them and struck them down. The mountains shook, \q and their corpses lay like trash in the middle of the streets. \q In spite of all this, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger has not turned back; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand is still stretched out.

L.25: Therefore the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has burned against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand against them and struck them, and the mountains quaked, \q and their corpses were like refuse in the middle of the streets. \q For all this {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger has not turned back, \q and still {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand [is] stretched out.

R.25: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is very angry with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. He has raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand to punish them and has struck them down. The mountains shook. \q Dead bodies lay in the streets like garbage. \q But even after all this, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is still angry. \q His hand is still raised to punish them.

decisions.choice: for all this his anger has not turned back: a refrain
decisions.reason: The same line ends the sections at 9:11, 9:16, 9:20 and 10:4. It says that past blows have not yet ended God's judgment, because the people have not turned back to him (9:12).

decisions.choice: has stretched out ... struck ... quaked: past blows, perhaps an earthquake
decisions.reason: The verbs describe what has already happened. The quaking mountains may recall the earthquake in the days of King Uzziah (Amos 1:1; Zechariah 14:5), or describe God's coming in judgment (Psalm 18:8).

decisions.choice: his hand stretched out: God's power to strike
decisions.reason: The stretched-out hand that once struck Egypt (Exodus 7:5; 15:12) is now raised against God's own people.

decisions.choice: to punish them
decisions.reason: Readable says why the hand is raised.

records.source: וְנָֽשָׂא־נֵ֤ס לַגּוֹיִם֙ מֵרָח֔וֹק וְשָׁ֥רַק ל֖וֹ מִקְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֥ה מְהֵרָ֖ה קַ֥ל יָבֽוֹא׃
records.gloss: And he will lift up a banner for [the] nations from afar, and he will whistle for it from [the] end of the earth; and look, quickly, swiftly it will come.
pieces: He will raise a signal flag for the nations far away and whistle to call them from the ends of the earth. \q And see, they come at full speed!

L.26: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lift up a banner for the nations from afar, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will whistle for it from the end of the earth; \q and look, quickly, swiftly it will come!

R.26: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will raise a flag to call nations from far away. He will whistle for them from the far ends of the earth. \q Look! They are coming fast!

decisions.choice: banner ... whistle: signals that call an army
decisions.reason: A banner on a pole set up on a hill was a rallying sign for troops (13:2; 18:3). The whistle is the call of a beekeeper or herdsman (7:18). God calls a foreign army as easily as a man calls his animals.

decisions.choice: nations ... it: many nations, or one nation
decisions.reason: "Nations" is plural, but "it will come" is singular, so one nation is meant, made up of many peoples. In Isaiah's day that nation was Assyria (7:18-20; 10:5), though it is not named here (compare Jeremiah 5:15).

decisions.choice: them / they
decisions.reason: The singular "it" refers to the army from "the nations"; Balanced and Readable say "they" so that the sentence reads clearly. Literal keeps "it".

decisions.choice: The LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as the subject from verse 25.

records.source: אֵין־עָיֵ֤ף וְאֵין־כּוֹשֵׁל֙ בּ֔וֹ לֹ֥א יָנ֖וּם וְלֹ֣א יִישָׁ֑ן וְלֹ֤א נִפְתַּח֙ אֵז֣וֹר חֲלָצָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א נִתַּ֖ק שְׂר֥וֹךְ נְעָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: There is no weary [one] and no [one] stumbling in it; not it will slumber and not it will sleep; and not will be opened [the] belt of its loins, and not will be snapped [the] thong of its sandals,
pieces: Among them no one is weary, no one trips; they do not nod off or fall asleep. \q No soldier's belt is untied at the waist, no strap of a sandal snaps.

L.27: There is none weary and none stumbling in it; none slumbers and none sleeps; \q and the belt of its waist is not loosened, and the strap of its sandals is not snapped,

R.27: None of their soldiers get tired or trip. None of them get sleepy. \q Their belts stay tight. Their sandal straps do not break.

decisions.choice: belt and sandal strap: ready for the march
decisions.reason: A soldier tightened his belt to be ready for action (1 Kings 18:46; Isaiah 11:5). Nothing in this army is loose or broken; it is fully prepared.

decisions.choice: soldier's / their soldiers
decisions.reason: The singular "it" is the army; Balanced and Readable name the soldiers.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֤ר חִצָּיו֙ שְׁנוּנִ֔ים וְכָל־קַשְּׁתֹתָ֖יו דְּרֻכ֑וֹת פַּרְס֤וֹת סוּסָיו֙ כַּצַּ֣ר נֶחְשָׁ֔בוּ וְגַלְגִּלָּ֖יו כַּסּוּפָֽה׃
records.gloss: whose arrows [are] sharpened and all its bows bent; [the] hooves of its horses like flint are regarded, and its wheels like the storm wind.
pieces: Their arrows have keen points, and every bow is drawn back ready. \q The hoofs of their horses are counted as hard as flint; the wheels of their chariots whirl like a storm wind.

L.28: whose arrows [are] sharpened, and all its bows bent; \q the hooves of its horses are regarded as flint, and its wheels like the storm wind.

R.28: Their arrows are sharp. Their bows are ready to shoot. \q Their horses' hoofs are as hard as stone. The wheels of their chariots turn fast like a storm.

decisions.choice: hooves like flint: horses that do not go lame
decisions.reason: Horses were not shod in Isaiah's day, so hard hooves were prized for long marches over rough ground.

decisions.choice: bows bent: bows strung and drawn
decisions.reason: The verb means to tread: a bow was bent by putting a foot on it to string it.

decisions.choice: chariots
decisions.reason: The wheels are those of war chariots; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: שְׁאָגָ֥ה ל֖וֹ כַּלָּבִ֑יא יִשְׁאַ֨ג כַּכְּפִירִ֤ים וְיִנְהֹם֙ וְיֹאחֵ֣ז טֶ֔רֶף וְיַפְלִ֖יט וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: Roaring [belongs] to it like a lion, it roars like the young lions; and it growls and seizes prey and carries [it] off, and there is no one rescuing.
pieces: The roar they raise is like a lion's; \q they roar like young lions. Growling, they take hold of the prey and drag it away, and there is no one to snatch it back.

L.29: Roaring [belongs] to it like a lion; \q it roars like the young lions; and it growls and seizes prey and carries [it] off, and there is none rescuing.

R.29: They roar like a lion. \q They roar like young lions that are hunting. They growl and grab their prey. They carry it away, and no one can save it.

decisions.choice: it roars: the reading in the margin
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text as written has a slightly different form of the verb, and the scribes' note in the margin gives this one. The meaning is the same: the army roars.

decisions.choice: lion: perhaps a lioness
decisions.reason: The word can mean a lion or a lioness. The picture is of a hunting lion that seizes its prey and carries it off to its den.

decisions.choice: no one rescuing: no help against this enemy
decisions.reason: No one can rescue Israel from the army God has called (Hosea 5:14; Micah 5:7). The prey is God's own people.

records.source: וְיִנְהֹ֥ם עָלָ֛יו בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כְּנַהֲמַת־יָ֑ם וְנִבַּ֤ט לָאָ֨רֶץ֙ וְהִנֵּה־חֹ֔שֶׁךְ צַ֣ר וָא֔וֹר חָשַׁ֖ךְ בַּעֲרִיפֶֽיהָ׃פ
records.gloss: And it will growl over it in day the that like [the] growling of [the] sea; and one will look to the land, and look, darkness, distress, and light has grown dark in its clouds.
pieces: On that day they will growl over their prey like the roaring of the sea. \q Look out over the land: there is darkness and distress, and the light has grown dark in its clouds.

L.30: And it will growl over it in that day like the growling of the sea; \q and [if] one looks to the land, look, darkness [and] distress, and [the] light has grown dark in its clouds.

R.30: At that time the enemy will growl over their prey like the roaring sea. \q Anyone who looks at the land will see only darkness and trouble. Even the light will be hidden by dark clouds.

decisions.choice: the growling of the sea: a picture of chaos
decisions.reason: The roaring sea stands for the powers that threaten God's people (17:12-13; Psalm 46:3-4).

decisions.choice: darkness, distress, and light: how the words go together
decisions.reason: The words can be read as "darkness and distress", or as "darkness of distress", or the first may go with the light: "distress, and even the light is darkened". The sense is the same: no hope of light (8:22).

decisions.choice: its clouds: a rare word
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It most likely means clouds or the dark sky over the land.

decisions.choice: their prey / the enemy
decisions.reason: "Over it" means over the prey of verse 29; Balanced and Readable say so, and Readable names the enemy army as the subject.
